title: Versuche über Pflanzen-Hybriden
authors: Mendel G
venue: Verhandlungen des naturforschenden Vereines in Brünn 4:3-47
summary: Pea-hybrid crossing experiments establishing that discrete hereditary factors segregate and assort independently, founding genetics.

title: Ueber die chemische Zusammensetzung der Eiterzellen
authors: Miescher F
summary: Isolated a phosphorus-rich, non-protein substance from leucocyte nuclei that he called nuclein, the first description of DNA as a chemical entity.

title: The chromosomes in heredity
authors: Sutton WS
summary: Proposed that Mendelian hereditary factors reside on chromosomes, uniting cytology with genetics in the chromosome theory of inheritance.

title: Artificial transmutation of the gene
authors: Muller HJ
summary: Showed X-rays greatly increase mutation rate in Drosophila, proving genes are physical structures that can be altered experimentally.

title: Sex limited inheritance in Drosophila
authors: Morgan TH
summary: The white-eye mutant linked a specific trait to the X chromosome, giving the first direct experimental evidence that genes lie on chromosomes.

title: The significance of pneumococcal types
authors: Griffith F
summary: Discovered bacterial transformation: heat-killed virulent pneumococci conferred their type on live avirulent cells, implying a transmissible 'transforming principle'.

title: Genetic control of biochemical reactions in Neurospora
authors: Beadle GW, Tatum EL
summary: Nutritional mutants of Neurospora established the one gene–one enzyme hypothesis, tying genes directly to specific biochemical steps.

title: Studies on the chemical nature of the substance inducing transformation of pneumococcal types
authors: Avery OT, MacLeod CM, McCarty M
summary: Purified Griffith's transforming principle and identified it as DNA, the first strong evidence that DNA is the hereditary material.

title: Chemical specificity of nucleic acids and mechanism of their enzymatic degradation
authors: Chargaff E
summary: Established that in DNA adenine equals thymine and guanine equals cytosine while base composition varies between species, the key constraint behind base pairing.

title: Independent functions of viral protein and nucleic acid in growth of bacteriophage
authors: Hershey AD, Chase M
summary: Radioisotope labelling of phage showed DNA, not protein, enters the host and carries genetic information, settling the question Avery had opened.

title: Molecular configuration in sodium thymonucleate
authors: Franklin R, Gosling RG
summary: X-ray fibre diffraction of B-form DNA (including Photo 51) giving the helical parameters and phosphate-outside geometry that constrained the double helix.

title: Molecular structure of nucleic acids: a structure for deoxyribose nucleic acid
authors: Watson JD, Crick FHC
summary: The antiparallel double helix with complementary A-T and G-C base pairs, immediately suggesting a copying mechanism for heredity.

title: Enzymatic synthesis of deoxyribonucleic acid
authors: Kornberg A, Lehman IR, Bessman MJ, Simms ES
summary: First template-dependent enzymatic synthesis of DNA in vitro, the discovery of DNA polymerase and the start of in vitro nucleic acid biochemistry.

title: The replication of DNA in Escherichia coli
authors: Meselson M, Stahl FW
summary: Density-gradient labelling showed DNA replicates semiconservatively, confirming the strand-separation prediction of the double helix.

title: On protein synthesis
authors: Crick FHC
venue: Symposia of the Society for Experimental Biology 12:138-163
summary: Set out the sequence hypothesis, the adaptor hypothesis and the central dogma of information flow from DNA to RNA to protein.

title: An unstable intermediate carrying information from genes to ribosomes for protein synthesis
authors: Brenner S, Jacob F, Meselson M
summary: Demonstrated a short-lived RNA messenger that carries genetic information to pre-existing ribosomes, establishing mRNA.

title: Genetic regulatory mechanisms in the synthesis of proteins
authors: Jacob F, Monod J
summary: The operon model of coordinated gene regulation by repressors acting on operators, founding the study of gene expression control.

title: The dependence of cell-free protein synthesis in E. coli upon naturally occurring or synthetic polyribonucleotides
authors: Nirenberg MW, Matthaei JH
summary: Poly(U) directed synthesis of polyphenylalanine in a cell-free extract, cracking the first codon and opening the way to the genetic code.

title: General nature of the genetic code for proteins
authors: Crick FHC, Barnett L, Brenner S, Watts-Tobin RJ
summary: Frameshift mutant analysis in phage T4 showed the code is read in non-overlapping triplets from a fixed starting point.

title: RNA codewords and protein synthesis: the effect of trinucleotides upon the binding of sRNA to ribosomes
authors: Nirenberg M, Leder P
summary: The triplet-binding assay that allowed systematic assignment of codons and, with Khorana's synthetic polymers, completion of the genetic code.

title: Structure of a ribonucleic acid
authors: Holley RW, Apgar J, Everett GA, Madison JT, Marquisee M, Merrill SH, et al.
summary: First complete sequence of a nucleic acid, yeast alanine tRNA, identifying the adaptor molecule Crick had postulated.

title: RNA-dependent DNA polymerase in virions of Rous sarcoma virus
authors: Temin HM, Mizutani S
summary: Discovery of reverse transcriptase in an RNA tumour virus, showing information can flow from RNA back to DNA.

title: RNA-dependent DNA polymerase in virions of RNA tumour viruses
authors: Baltimore D
summary: Independent demonstration of reverse transcriptase, the enzyme that later made cDNA cloning and much of molecular biology possible.

title: Spliced segments at the 5' terminus of adenovirus 2 late mRNA
authors: Berget SM, Moore C, Sharp PA
summary: Showed mRNA is assembled from discontinuous genomic segments, revealing RNA splicing and introns in eukaryotic gene expression.

title: DNA restriction enzyme from E. coli
authors: Meselson M, Yuan R
summary: Isolated the first restriction enzyme activity, giving biochemical substance to Arber's host-controlled restriction and modification.

title: A restriction enzyme from Hemophilus influenzae. I. Purification and general properties
authors: Smith HO, Wilcox KW
summary: Purified HindII, the first sequence-specific restriction endonuclease, providing the molecular scissors that made DNA cloning possible.

title: Specific cleavage of simian virus 40 DNA by restriction endonuclease of Hemophilus influenzae
authors: Danna K, Nathans D
summary: Used a restriction enzyme to cut a viral genome into defined fragments, producing the first physical restriction map of a DNA molecule.

title: Enzymatic breakage and joining of deoxyribonucleic acid, I. Repair of single-strand breaks in DNA by an enzyme from E. coli infected with T4 bacteriophage
authors: Weiss B, Richardson CC
summary: Characterised DNA ligase, the enzyme that seals DNA backbones and became the essential joining reagent of recombinant DNA work.

title: Biochemical method for inserting new genetic information into DNA of simian virus 40: circular SV40 DNA molecules containing lambda phage genes and the galactose operon of Escherichia coli
authors: Jackson DA, Symons RH, Berg P
summary: First construction of a recombinant DNA molecule in vitro, joining viral and bacterial DNA and creating the field of genetic engineering.

title: Construction of biologically functional bacterial plasmids in vitro
authors: Cohen SN, Chang AC, Boyer HW, Helling RB
summary: Built recombinant plasmids that replicated and expressed their inserted genes in E. coli, making molecular cloning a practical, general technology.

title: Summary statement of the Asilomar Conference on recombinant DNA molecules
authors: Berg P, Baltimore D, Brenner S, Roblin RO, Singer MF
summary: The Asilomar consensus on containment-based self-governance of recombinant DNA research, the template for later biotechnology governance.

title: Process for producing biologically functional molecular chimeras (US Patent 4,237,224)
authors: Cohen SN, Boyer HW
venue: United States Patent and Trademark Office
summary: The Cohen-Boyer gene-splicing patent, licensed broadly to industry and the commercial foundation of the biotechnology sector.

title: Detection of specific sequences among DNA fragments separated by gel electrophoresis
authors: Southern EM
summary: The Southern blot: transfer of electrophoresed DNA to a membrane and detection by hybridisation, the workhorse assay of early gene analysis.

title: Expression in Escherichia coli of a chemically synthesized gene for the hormone somatostatin
authors: Itakura K, Hirose T, Crea R, Riggs AD, Heyneker HL, Bolivar F, et al.
summary: First bacterial expression of a chemically synthesised gene encoding a human peptide hormone, the proof of concept for recombinant pharmaceuticals.

title: Mutagenesis at a specific position in a DNA sequence
authors: Hutchison CA 3rd, Phillips S, Edgell MH, Gillam S, Jahnke P, Smith M
summary: Used a synthetic mismatched oligonucleotide to introduce a predetermined point mutation, inventing oligonucleotide-directed site-specific mutagenesis.

title: Enzymatic amplification of beta-globin genomic sequences and restriction site analysis for diagnosis of sickle cell anemia
authors: Saiki RK, Scharf S, Faloona F, Mullis KB, Horn GT, Erlich HA, et al.
summary: First published application of the polymerase chain reaction, amplifying a human gene segment for genetic diagnosis.

title: Primer-directed enzymatic amplification of DNA with a thermostable DNA polymerase
authors: Saiki RK, Gelfand DH, Stoffel S, Scharf SJ, Higuchi R, Horn GT, et al.
summary: Introduced Taq polymerase into PCR, giving specificity, long products and automation and turning PCR into universal laboratory infrastructure.

title: Green fluorescent protein as a marker for gene expression
authors: Chalfie M, Tu Y, Euskirchen G, Ward WW, Prasher DC
summary: Showed GFP fluoresces when expressed heterologously, creating a genetically encoded reporter that transformed cell and developmental biology.

title: Genetic transformation of mouse embryos by microinjection of purified DNA
authors: Gordon JW, Scangos GA, Plotkin DJ, Barbosa JA, Ruddle FH
summary: First transgenic mice made by pronuclear microinjection, extending recombinant DNA from microbes to whole animals.

title: Dramatic growth of mice that develop from eggs microinjected with metallothionein-growth hormone fusion genes
authors: Palmiter RD, Brinster RL, Hammer RE, Trumbauer ME, Rosenfeld MG, Birnberg NC, et al.
summary: A regulated transgene produced a dramatic whole-animal phenotype, establishing transgenic animals as tools for studying gene function and expression.

title: Insertion of DNA sequences into the human chromosomal beta-globin locus by homologous recombination
authors: Smithies O, Gregg RG, Boggs SS, Koralewski MA, Kucherlapati RS
summary: Showed exogenous DNA can be targeted to a chosen chromosomal locus in mammalian cells by homologous recombination, the origin of gene targeting.

title: Site-directed mutagenesis by gene targeting in mouse embryo-derived stem cells
authors: Thomas KR, Capecchi MR
summary: Gene targeting in embryonic stem cells, the route to knockout mice and to systematic reverse genetics in mammals.

title: Filamentous fusion phage: novel expression vectors that display cloned antigens on the virion surface
authors: Smith GP
summary: Invented phage display, physically linking a peptide to the gene encoding it so vast libraries can be selected by binding.

title: Phage antibodies: filamentous phage displaying antibody variable domains
authors: McCafferty J, Griffiths AD, Winter G, Chiswell DJ
summary: Displayed antibody fragments on phage, enabling fully in vitro selection of human antibodies and a generation of antibody drugs.

title: Tuning the activity of an enzyme for unusual environments: sequential random mutagenesis of subtilisin E for catalysis in dimethylformamide
authors: Chen K, Arnold FH
summary: Iterated rounds of random mutagenesis and screening improved an enzyme far beyond rational design, establishing directed evolution of proteins.

title: Rapid evolution of a protein in vitro by DNA shuffling
authors: Stemmer WPC
summary: Added in vitro recombination to directed evolution, letting beneficial mutations from different variants be combined efficiently.

title: Introduction of double-strand breaks into the genome of mouse cells by expression of a rare-cutting endonuclease
authors: Rouet P, Smih F, Jasin M
summary: Showed a targeted double-strand break made by a meganuclease greatly stimulates recombination at that site, the founding principle of nuclease-based genome editing.

title: Hybrid restriction enzymes: zinc finger fusions to Fok I cleavage domain
authors: Kim YG, Cha J, Chandrasegaran S
summary: Fused programmable zinc-finger DNA-binding domains to a nuclease domain, creating the first designer nucleases (ZFNs).

title: Highly efficient endogenous human gene correction using designed zinc-finger nucleases
authors: Urnov FD, Miller JC, Lee YL, Beausejour CM, Rock JM, Augustus S, et al.
summary: Efficient correction of an endogenous human disease gene in cultured cells, showing therapeutic genome editing was feasible.

title: Breaking the code of DNA binding specificity of TAL-type III effectors
authors: Boch J, Scholze H, Schornack S, Landgraf A, Hahn S, Kay S, et al.
summary: Independently cracked and experimentally validated the TAL effector recognition code, enabling custom DNA-binding protein design.

title: A TALE nuclease architecture for efficient genome editing
authors: Miller JC, Tan S, Qiao G, Barlow KA, Wang J, Xia DF, et al.
summary: Built TALE nucleases that edit endogenous human genes efficiently, giving an easier-to-design alternative to ZFNs.

title: Nucleotide sequence of the iap gene, responsible for alkaline phosphatase isozyme conversion in Escherichia coli, and identification of the gene product
authors: Ishino Y, Shinagawa H, Makino K, Amemura M, Nakata A
summary: Incidentally reported the first CRISPR array: an unexplained set of interspaced repeats downstream of the E. coli iap gene.

title: Identification of genes that are associated with DNA repeats in prokaryotes
authors: Jansen R, van Embden JDA, Gaastra W, Schouls LM
summary: Named CRISPR and the associated cas genes, recognising the repeat family as a coherent, widespread prokaryotic system.

title: Intervening sequences of regularly spaced prokaryotic repeats derive from foreign genetic elements
authors: Mojica FJM, Díez-Villaseñor C, García-Martínez J, Soria E
summary: Found that CRISPR spacers match phage and plasmid sequences, and proposed CRISPR is a prokaryotic adaptive immune system.

title: CRISPR provides acquired resistance against viruses in prokaryotes
authors: Barrangou R, Fremaux C, Deveau H, Richards M, Boyaval P, Moineau S, et al.
summary: Experimental proof that spacer acquisition confers heritable, sequence-specific phage resistance requiring cas genes.

title: Small CRISPR RNAs guide antiviral defense in prokaryotes
authors: Brouns SJJ, Jore MM, Lundgren M, Westra ER, Slijkhuis RJH, Snijders APL, et al.
summary: Showed CRISPR arrays are processed into small guide RNAs that direct Cas protein complexes to invader nucleic acid.

title: CRISPR interference limits horizontal gene transfer in staphylococci by targeting DNA
authors: Marraffini LA, Sontheimer EJ
summary: Established that CRISPR systems target DNA rather than RNA, a prerequisite for using them as genome-editing tools.

title: The CRISPR/Cas bacterial immune system cleaves bacteriophage and plasmid DNA
authors: Garneau JE, Dupuis MÈ, Villion M, Romero DA, Barrangou R, Boyaval P, et al.
summary: Showed Cas9 introduces precise double-strand breaks in target DNA in vivo, identifying the enzyme later used for editing.

title: CRISPR RNA maturation by trans-encoded small RNA and host factor RNase III
authors: Deltcheva E, Chylinski K, Sharma CM, Gonzales K, Chao Y, Pirzada ZA, et al.
summary: Discovered tracrRNA and its role in crRNA maturation, the missing component of the two-RNA Cas9 system.

title: A programmable dual-RNA-guided DNA endonuclease in adaptive bacterial immunity
authors: Jinek M, Chylinski K, Fonfara I, Hauer M, Doudna JA, Charpentier E
summary: Reconstituted Cas9 cleavage in vitro and showed a single chimeric guide RNA can be programmed to cut any chosen DNA sequence.

title: Cas9-crRNA ribonucleoprotein complex mediates specific DNA cleavage for adaptive immunity in bacteria
authors: Gasiunas G, Barrangou R, Horvath P, Siksnys V
summary: Independently reconstituted programmable Cas9-crRNA cleavage and defined the PAM requirement and cut-site geometry.

title: Multiplex genome engineering using CRISPR/Cas systems
authors: Cong L, Ran FA, Cox D, Lin S, Barretto R, Habib N, et al.
summary: Engineered Cas9 for mammalian cells and showed efficient multiplexed editing of human and mouse genomes.

title: RNA-guided human genome engineering via Cas9
authors: Mali P, Yang L, Esvelt KM, Aach J, Guell M, DiCarlo JE, et al.
summary: Demonstrated RNA-guided editing and homology-directed repair in human cells, including stem cells, with a simple guide-RNA toolkit.

title: Repurposing CRISPR as an RNA-guided platform for sequence-specific control of gene expression
authors: Qi LS, Larson MH, Gilbert LA, Doudna JA, Weissman JS, Arkin AP, et al.
summary: Catalytically dead Cas9 used as a programmable DNA-binding module (CRISPRi), separating targeting from cutting.

title: Genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screening in human cells
authors: Shalem O, Sanjana NE, Hartenian E, Shi X, Scott DA, Mikkelson T, et al.
summary: Pooled genome-wide guide libraries turned editing into a forward-genetic screening platform in human cells.

title: Epigenome editing by a CRISPR-Cas9-based acetyltransferase activates genes from promoters and enhancers
authors: Hilton IB, D'Ippolito AM, Vockley CM, Thakore PI, Crawford GE, Reddy TE, et al.
summary: Targeted a chromatin-modifying enzyme with dCas9 to switch on endogenous genes, founding programmable epigenome editing.

title: Cpf1 is a single RNA-guided endonuclease of a class 2 CRISPR-Cas system
authors: Zetsche B, Gootenberg JS, Abudayyeh OO, Slaymaker IM, Makarova KS, Essletzbichler P, et al.
summary: Characterised Cas12a (Cpf1), a single-RNA-guided nuclease with a different PAM and staggered cuts, broadening the editing toolbox.

title: Programmable editing of a target base in genomic DNA without double-stranded DNA cleavage
authors: Komor AC, Kim YB, Packer MS, Zuris JA, Liu DR
summary: Fused a cytidine deaminase to dCas9 to convert C to T directly, inventing base editing without double-strand breaks.

title: Programmable base editing of A·T to G·C in genomic DNA without DNA cleavage
authors: Gaudelli NM, Komor AC, Rees HA, Packer MS, Badran AH, Bryson DI, et al.
summary: Evolved an adenine deaminase that does not exist in nature to make A-to-G base editors, covering the most common pathogenic point mutations.

title: RNA targeting with CRISPR-Cas13a
authors: Abudayyeh OO, Gootenberg JS, Essletzbichler P, Han S, Joung J, Belanto JJ, et al.
summary: Used Cas13 for programmable knockdown and editing of RNA in mammalian cells, extending CRISPR beyond DNA.

title: Search-and-replace genome editing without double-strand breaks or donor DNA
authors: Anzalone AV, Randolph PB, Davis JR, Sousa AA, Koblan LW, Levy JM, et al.
summary: Prime editing: a Cas9 nickase fused to reverse transcriptase writes new sequence from an extended guide RNA, enabling insertions, deletions and all base changes.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing for sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia
authors: Frangoul H, Altshuler D, Cappellini MD, Chen YS, Domm J, Eustace BK, et al.
summary: Ex vivo CRISPR editing of BCL11A in patient stem cells produced transfusion independence and freedom from crises, the first clear clinical cures by genome editing.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 in vivo gene editing for transthyretin amyloidosis
authors: Gillmore JD, Gane E, Taubel J, Kao J, Fontana M, Maitland ML, et al.
summary: First demonstration that lipid-nanoparticle-delivered CRISPR can knock out a disease gene in the human liver in vivo.

title: Approval of exagamglogene autotemcel (Casgevy), the first CRISPR-based therapy
authors: US Food and Drug Administration
venue: FDA Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research approval announcement
summary: Regulatory approval of a CRISPR-edited cell therapy for sickle cell disease, eleven years after the Cas9 programmability papers.

title: Bridge RNAs direct programmable recombination of target and donor DNA
authors: Durrant MG, Perry NT, Pai JJ, Jangid AR, Athukoralage JS, Hiraizumi M, et al.
summary: IS110 insertion sequences use a bicistronic bridge RNA specifying both target and donor, giving a programmable recombinase that inserts, inverts and excises DNA.

title: Patient-specific in vivo gene editing to treat a rare genetic disease
authors: Musunuru K, Grandinette SA, Wang X, Hudson TR, Briseno K, Berry AM, et al.
summary: A bespoke in vivo base-editing therapy designed and dosed for one infant with CPS1 deficiency, the first personalised genome-editing medicine.

title: Construction of a genetic toggle switch in Escherichia coli
authors: Gardner TS, Cantor CR, Collins JJ
summary: Built a bistable genetic switch from mutually repressing promoters, the first designed, model-driven synthetic gene circuit.

title: A synthetic oscillatory network of transcriptional regulators
authors: Elowitz MB, Leibler S
summary: The repressilator, a three-repressor ring that oscillates in single cells, showing that dynamic behaviour can be designed from parts.

title: Idempotent vector design for standard assembly of BioBricks
authors: Knight TF
venue: MIT Synthetic Biology Working Group Technical Report
summary: Defined the BioBrick standard prefix/suffix assembly scheme, introducing interchangeable parts and engineering abstraction to biology.

title: Production of the antimalarial drug precursor artemisinic acid in engineered yeast
authors: Ro DK, Paradise EM, Ouellet M, Fisher KJ, Newman KL, Ndungu JM, et al.
summary: Rebuilt a plant terpenoid pathway in yeast to make artemisinic acid, the landmark demonstration of metabolic engineering for a drug.

title: High-level semi-synthetic production of the potent antimalarial artemisinin
authors: Paddon CJ, Westfall PJ, Pitera DJ, Benjamin K, Fisher K, McPhee D, et al.
summary: Scaled engineered yeast plus chemical conversion to industrial semi-synthetic artemisinin, the first commercial synthetic-biology drug supply.

title: Enzymatic assembly of DNA molecules up to several hundred kilobases
authors: Gibson DG, Young L, Chuang RY, Venter JC, Hutchison CA 3rd, Smith HO
summary: Gibson assembly: isothermal, scarless one-pot joining of overlapping DNA fragments, now the default method for building large constructs.

title: Creation of a bacterial cell controlled by a chemically synthesized genome
authors: Gibson DG, Glass JI, Lartigue C, Noskov VN, Chuang RY, Algire MA, et al.
summary: JCVI-syn1.0: a 1.08 Mb chemically synthesised Mycoplasma genome transplanted into a recipient cell that then self-replicated, the first synthetic-genome organism.

title: Design and synthesis of a minimal bacterial genome
authors: Hutchison CA 3rd, Chuang RY, Noskov VN, Assad-Garcia N, Deerinck TJ, Ellisman MH, et al.
summary: JCVI-syn3.0, a 531 kb designed genome with 473 genes, defining a near-minimal self-replicating cell and exposing many genes of unknown function.

title: Total synthesis of a functional designer eukaryotic chromosome
authors: Annaluru N, Muller H, Mitchell LA, Ramalingam S, Stracquadanio G, Richardson SM, et al.
summary: synIII, the first synthetic eukaryotic chromosome, redesigned with loxPsym sites for inducible genome scrambling and functional in yeast.

title: Programming cells by multiplex genome engineering and accelerated evolution
authors: Wang HH, Isaacs FJ, Carr PA, Sun ZZ, Xu G, Forest CR, et al.
summary: MAGE used pools of oligonucleotides to edit many genomic sites simultaneously and iteratively, enabling combinatorial genome-scale optimisation.

title: A general method for site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids into proteins
authors: Noren CJ, Anthony-Cahill SJ, Griffith MC, Schultz PG
summary: Chemically acylated suppressor tRNA allowed non-natural amino acids to be read into proteins in vitro, the start of genetic code expansion.

title: Expanding the genetic code of Escherichia coli
authors: Wang L, Brock A, Herrick B, Schultz PG
summary: An orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pair let living bacteria incorporate an unnatural amino acid in response to a reassigned codon.

title: A semi-synthetic organism with an expanded genetic alphabet
authors: Malyshev DA, Dhami K, Lavergne T, Chen T, Dai N, Foster JM, et al.
summary: A bacterium stably propagated a third, unnatural base pair in its DNA, extending the chemical alphabet of heredity.

title: Total synthesis of Escherichia coli with a recoded genome
authors: Fredens J, Wang K, de la Torre D, Funke LFH, Robertson WE, Christova Y, et al.
summary: Syn61: a 4 Mb synthetic E. coli genome using 61 rather than 64 codons, freeing codons for genetic code expansion and virus resistance.

title: A system for the continuous directed evolution of biomolecules
authors: Esvelt KM, Carlson JC, Liu DR
summary: Phage-assisted continuous evolution (PACE) links a desired activity to phage propagation, running hundreds of evolution rounds per week.

title: Complete biosynthesis of opioids in yeast
authors: Galanie S, Thodey K, Trenchard IJ, Filsinger Interrante M, Smolke CD
summary: Reconstituted more than twenty plant, mammalian and microbial enzymes in yeast to make opioids from sugar, a benchmark in long-pathway engineering and its governance.

title: Rapid, low-cost detection of Zika virus using programmable biomolecular components
authors: Pardee K, Green AA, Takahashi MK, Braff D, Lambert G, Lee JW, et al.
summary: Freeze-dried cell-free gene circuits on paper gave programmable, field-deployable diagnostics, bringing synthetic biology out of the cell.

title: Nucleic acid detection with CRISPR-Cas13a/C2c2
authors: Gootenberg JS, Abudayyeh OO, Lee JW, Essletzbichler P, Dy AJ, Joung J, et al.
summary: SHERLOCK coupled Cas13 collateral cleavage to isothermal amplification for attomolar nucleic acid detection, later used for SARS-CoV-2 tests.

title: Concerning RNA-guided gene drives for the alteration of wild populations
authors: Esvelt KM, Smidler AL, Catteruccia F, Church GM
summary: Proposed CRISPR-based gene drives that spread through wild populations, together with containment strategies and a call for public deliberation.

title: A CRISPR-Cas9 gene drive targeting doublesex causes complete population suppression in caged Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes
authors: Kyrou K, Hammond AM, Galizi R, Kranjc N, Burt A, Beaghton AK, et al.
summary: A drive targeting a conserved sex-determination gene collapsed caged malaria-mosquito populations without resistance arising, the strongest suppression-drive result to date.

title: Stable incorporation of plasmid DNA into higher plant cells: the molecular basis of crown gall tumorigenesis
authors: Chilton MD, Drummond MH, Merlo DJ, Sciaky D, Montoya AL, Gordon MP, et al.
summary: Showed Agrobacterium transfers Ti-plasmid DNA into the plant genome, revealing nature's own plant transformation vector.

title: Expression of chimaeric genes transferred into plant nuclei using a Ti-plasmid-derived vector
authors: Herrera-Estrella L, Depicker A, Van Montagu M, Schell J
summary: Disarmed Ti plasmids delivered and expressed a selectable chimaeric gene in plant nuclei, creating the first transgenic plants.

title: A simple and general method for transferring genes into plants
authors: Horsch RB, Fry JE, Hoffmann NL, Eichholtz D, Rogers SG, Fraley RT
summary: The leaf-disc transformation protocol that made routine production of transgenic plants practical for laboratories everywhere.

title: High-velocity microprojectiles for delivering nucleic acids into living cells
authors: Klein TM, Wolf ED, Wu R, Sanford JC
summary: The gene gun delivered DNA into cells physically, opening transformation of cereals and organelles that Agrobacterium could not reach.

title: Engineering herbicide tolerance in transgenic plants
authors: Shah DM, Horsch RB, Klee HJ, Kishore GM, Winter JA, Tumer NE, et al.
summary: Overexpression of an EPSP synthase gene gave glyphosate tolerance, the research line that became Roundup Ready crops.

title: Transgenic plants protected from insect attack
authors: Vaeck M, Reynaerts A, Höfte H, Jansens S, De Beuckeleer M, Dean C, et al.
summary: Expressed a Bacillus thuringiensis toxin gene in tobacco to kill feeding larvae, the origin of Bt insect-resistant crops.

title: Reduction of polygalacturonase activity in tomato fruit by antisense RNA
authors: Sheehy RE, Kramer M, Hiatt WR
summary: Antisense suppression of a ripening enzyme slowed tomato softening, the science behind the Flavr Savr tomato.

title: FDA clearance of the Flavr Savr tomato, the first genetically engineered whole food
authors: US Food and Drug Administration
venue: US Food and Drug Administration decision; Calgene Inc.
summary: First regulatory clearance of a transgenic food crop for sale, setting the precedent for GM food review in the United States.

title: Engineering the provitamin A (beta-carotene) biosynthetic pathway into (carotenoid-free) rice endosperm
authors: Ye X, Al-Babili S, Klöti A, Zhang J, Lucca P, Beyer P, et al.
summary: Golden Rice: a multi-gene carotenoid pathway installed in rice endosperm, the flagship nutritional-biofortification transgenic crop.

title: Biocatalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral amines from ketones applied to sitagliptin manufacture
authors: Savile CK, Janey JM, Mundorff EC, Moore JC, Tam S, Jarvis WR, et al.
summary: A transaminase evolved far beyond its natural substrate range replaced a metal-catalysed step in a commercial drug process, the showcase of industrial directed evolution.

title: Precise genome modification in the crop species Zea mays using zinc-finger nucleases
authors: Shukla VK, Doyon Y, Miller JC, DeKelver RC, Moehle EA, Worden SE, et al.
summary: Brought designer-nuclease editing to a major crop, adding targeted trait insertion to random transgene integration.

title: High-efficiency TALEN-based gene editing produces disease-resistant rice
authors: Li T, Liu B, Spalding MH, Weeks DP, Yang B
summary: TALEN editing of a bacterial-blight susceptibility gene gave disease-resistant rice, an early transgene-free edited crop trait.

title: Targeted genome modification of crops using CRISPR/Cas systems
authors: Shan Q, Wang Y, Li J, Zhang Y, Chen K, Liang Z, et al.
summary: First CRISPR editing in crop plants (rice and wheat), which rapidly became the standard method of plant breeding research.

title: De novo domestication of wild tomato using genome editing
authors: Zsögön A, Čermák T, Naves ER, Notini MM, Edel KH, Weinl S, et al.
summary: Edited a handful of known domestication genes in a wild tomato to recreate crop traits directly, proposing de novo domestication as a breeding strategy.
